articles.title: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess
articles.summary: The SNL alum has an appealing energy and this is an improvement on the 2003 travesty but it’s also far too long and strangely corporate. Over a long enough timeline, perhaps every living alumnus of Saturday Night Live will play the Cat in the Hat.
body: Just to be clear, this is the same studio that passed on releasing not one but two well-liked features starring their trademark Looney Tunes characters in the last few years. (Puzzlingly, a new Looney Tunes short starring Daffy Duck nonetheless debuts in front of this movie.) Warner has one of the most storied animation libraries in American cinema (and, for that matter, plenty of great animated TV shows like Batman: The Animated Series and Animaniacs) but as far as features go, they’ve never settled on a clear creative vision. They seem just as adrift in a landscape crowded with serious competitors as they were back when everyone was imitating Disney.

When the Cat arrives, he eventually – the movie’s set-up, midsection and climax are all painfully distended – whisks the kids and their suddenly talking goldfish Waffles (Matt Berry, the other vocal MVP of the cast) into a series of magical lands expanded from the family’s possessions. They’re in search of the Cat’s Go-Backer device, which Gabby hopes to use to undo their family’s move, and pursued by a shadowy, gigantic creature called Something.
points: The SNL alum has an appealing energy and this is an improvement on the 2003 travesty but it’s also far too long and strangely corporate.

articles.title: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble
articles.summary: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera. Let’s hope not. A long time ago, far far away, in a galaxy called the 1970s, kids dreamed of joining the rebellion, rescuing a princess and blowing up…
body: It is worth remembering this when considering Florence Pugh’s recent declaration, ahead of next month’s Dune: Part Three, that Dune is her generation’s Star Wars. And then wondering how much trouble we might be in if she’s actually right. “I think they brought back movie-going. What an event the second [Dune] was,” Pugh cheerfully told the New York Times. “It was just so lovely to be a part of something that we know is our generational kind of Star Wars.”

Pugh’s analogy becomes stranger the more you think about it. Lucas may have drawn heavily on Frank Herbert’s original 1965 book when he dreamed up the desert planet of Tatooine, but the two sagas offer distinctly different views of the universe. The original Star Wars trilogy asked us to believe that its central villain was ultimately worthy of redemption, despite having been a powerful cog in a regime responsible for billions of deaths. Dune, by contrast, is flowing grimly in exactly the opposite direction.
points: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera.

articles.title: Alex Cooper, Matt Kaplan, Unwell Sign With CAA
articles.summary: Creative Artists Agency has signed Alex Cooper, Matt Kaplan, and their media and entertainment company Unwell for representation, a move that has been in discussions for weeks.
body: CAA will work with the duo to expand their business of Unwell, their content company, while supporting growth and the development of original intellectual property.

Cooper and Kaplan have expanded Unwell’s leadership team over the past year, adding seasoned executives to work alongside Chief Marketing Officer T.J. Marchetti: media and technology veteran Joanne Bradford as President; former NFL and Raine Group executive Samir Sama as Head of Ventures and Corporate Development; previous Meta and Disney executive Mina Lefevre as Chief Content Officer and Head of Television; former Misfits Gaming and Fox Networks Group executive Lagen Nash as Executive Vice President of Revenue; and former CAA agent Olivia Owen as Head of Talent.

Since launching in 2018, Cooper’s podcast has become known for featuring candid conversations with leading figures across entertainment, politics, sports, and culture. The show is distributed through a partnership with SiriusXM, which also powers the Unwell audio channel on SiriusXM’s satellite radio service.

articles.title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Grows in Syndication and Streaming as Season 44 Introduces New Gameplay (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: “Wheel of Fortune” introduced some new features for its Season 44, and it appears to be paying off with viewers. The long-running syndicated game show is averaging 8.59 million viewers in linear this year, up 17% from last year, while its household rating is a 4.8, up 16% from last year.
body: In Season 44, “Wheel of Fortune” gameplay added a new opening round, dubbed “Fortune Frenzy,” which follows contestants as they’re given 30 seconds to solve as many puzzles as possible. That means more puzzles at the start of the show.

Sony said the ratings increase also comes as it assumes marketing, promotions and affiliate relations for “Wheel.” A year ago, CBS Media Ventures and Sony Pictures TV settled their long-running battle over the distribution of “Wheel” and “Jeopardy.” As part of their settlement, Sony took over international distribution of “Wheel” last year, while CBS kept domestic distribution through 2027-2028 (at which point Sony takes it over). CBS continued to handle marketing, promotions and affiliate relations last year, but all of that moved to Sony starting this fall.

articles.title: Why Does Amazon Want a TV Show Starring Melania Trump?
articles.summary: Amazon, it seems, cannot get enough “Melania.” And at this moment, they feel like the only entity for whom that’s true. The company has announced its plan to release a two-part documentary series about First Lady Melania Trump on Nov.
body: Even by this family’s low standard, it seemed shameless: Melania Trump was willing to accept a staggeringly large check but seemed not to feel even the slightest twinge that would have prompted her to offer something, anything, to earn the fee. But the film was a document of an aesthetic, and a movement, that was ascendant.

Something’s shifted! Trump is still the president (and Melania still the first lady), but we’ve just been issued as striking notice as possible that whatever change Trump has lost control of the national conversation. (Notable, perhaps: “Melania” came out in theaters before the launch of the disastrous war in Iran, a turning point for the president’s popularity.) This ought to have been predictable: Beyond the fact that Trump’s own tendencies seemed likely to doom his popularity sooner or later, no moment in time lasts forever, and electoral victories are just that, not restructures of society at every level.

articles.title: ‘Mom encouraged me to get breast implants’: Disney child star Christy Carlson Romano on fame, family and freedom
articles.summary: She started acting at six and by 16 was starring in Even Stevens with Shia LaBeouf. Then her career fell apart. Here, she explains how she survived growing up in the spotlight. In a class at college, Christy Carlson Romano was encouraged to think about her “community”.
body: The title of her memoir, Once Upon a Trainwreck, gives you a flavour of where Carlson Romano, 42, is coming from, but what’s most striking isn’t that she goes off the rails (she doesn’t, hugely, compared to other former child stars), but how sensible and mature she is as a child. It’s alarming. When fans recognise her now – she was in the popular Disney series Even Stevens which started in 2000 – they tell her she was a huge part of their childhoods. She had been acting the part of a normal suburban girl, the perfectionist Ren Stevens, while having no idea what that was like. She was already a mini adult.

Now Carlson Romano has a social media career, which has given her a detachment from the entertainment industry. “I’m outspoken at this point, but for a lot of people they can’t do that,” she says. “What hurts is when I see other child actors suffering, because I know that means they haven’t found their way through the pain.” We speak, over Zoom, not long after Hayden Panettiere, the “Nashville” actor and singer who had started as a child and had talked about her experience of early fame, addiction and mental illness, had been found dead.

articles.title: ‘Too many stories exist only to make you think you’re on the right side’: Cristian Mungiu on Fjord, the Cannes winner that divided Europe
articles.summary: The Romanian auteur’s new film could have been the kind of homogenous ‘Europudding’ he’s railed against for years. Instead, it’s a culture-clash skewering of conservative and liberal values worthy of its Palme d’Or. ‘Pffff!” Cristian Mungiu lets out an exasperated sigh.
body: In 2013, Mungiu was part of a delegation of European auteurs who travelled to Brussels to meet the then president of the European Commission, José Manuel Barroso. At the time, the EU and US were in talks to slash barriers to trade between the two economic blocs, and the film-makers were lobbying the Commission to spare their industry from the deal.

If countries weren’t allowed to subsidise their own productions, one argument went, European cinema would become a stolid mush of homogenised co-productions – “Europudding”, as people called it at the time. To those ends, they would no longer be able to create national dramas like Mungiu’s own 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, a riveting abortion thriller set in cold war-era Bucharest that had won the Palme d’Or at Cannes in 2007.

articles.title: Brand's barrister refers himself to regulator after report he confronted journalist
articles.summary: Ian Winter allegedly confronted a reporter outside court who had investigated the comedian.
body: Russell Brand's defence barrister has referred himself to the regulator after reports that he confronted a Sunday Times journalist who was involved in a media investigation into Brand in 2023.
In a Times and Sunday Times podcast on Thursday, Rosamund Urwin said she introduced herself to Ian Winter KC outside court after verdicts were delivered.
She claimed he responded with a "snarl" and said "I hope you're pleased with yourself".
"Apparently I said, but I can't actually remember this but I've read it in reporting, 'I am pleased that justice has been done'", Urwin said.

articles.title: Met Police boss 'wouldn't be surprised' if more allegations made about Brand
articles.summary: Sir Mark Rowley tells the BBC that what he heard reported from Brand's trial came close to "victim blaming".
body: The head of the Metropolitan Police said he "wouldn't be surprised" if more people came forward to make allegations about entertainer and comedian Russell Brand.
On Thursday, Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
Met Police boss Sir Mark Rowley also told BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Friday that what he heard reported from Brand's trial at Southwark Crown Court came very close to "victim blaming".
Brand was acquitted of two other rape charges and one allegation of attempted indecent assault. The 51-year-old will be sentenced on Monday.

articles.title: George R.R. Martin Tapped for Lifetime Achievement Nod at Infinity Festival (Exclusive)
articles.summary: In addition, Pola Maneli, director of the animated short 'Apart,' co-written by Spike Lee, has joined the lineup for the previously announced ASIFA-Showcase.
body: George R.R. Martin has been tapped to receive the Monolith Lifetime Achievement Award at this year’s Infinity Festival.

Martin, creator of the A Song of Ice and Fire novels that inspired HBO’s Game of Thrones, will accept the award at the event, which is set to take place Nov. 12-15 at the Audrey Irmas Pavilion in Los Angeles.

Heirs of the Perisphere, directed by Chris Eyre and written by Caroline Spector, is based on a short story by Martin’s longtime friend, science-fiction author Howard Waldrop. The film follows three animatronic robots who awaken after centuries of silence to discover humanity has vanished and embark on a journey to find their creators.

The Monolith Lifetime Achievement Award recognizes “individuals whose contributions have left a lasting impact on entertainment,” organizers said. The festival will honor Martin’s “lifetime of storytelling and his dedication to bringing the work of his dear friend Howard Waldrop to the screen.”
